A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Text2Grad, with matching authors, core methods, benchmarks, and substantial overlapping content. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, policy-training results across summarization, code generation, and question answering, human annotation agreement, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, Mistral evaluations, reward-design ablations, and annotation quality and efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: Critique/span annotation, the autoregressive reward model, uniform positive/negative token rewards, and PPO optimization remain unchanged; Algorithms 1–4 are retained. Replacing 'dual-headed' with 'unified' matches the model already specified in v1 Section 3.4. Expanded grounding and tokenization descriptions disclose implementation details without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SLF5K, KodCode, and UltraFeedback, with the same summarization, HumanEval/MBPP and enhanced variants, AlpacaEval, ARC-Challenge, and MT-Bench coverage. The Mistral evaluation and feedback-source ablations reuse existing data and tasks; they expand model configurations and analyses.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 newly evaluate DPO and ILF across all three domains. PRM-PPO is added for summarization and code generation, and Dense Reward is added for summarization. These substantially broaden comparison beyond v1's PPO, SFT/reflection, and pretrained/proprietary references. PRM-PPO's stated exclusion from UltraFeedback is not a removal, since v1 did not evaluate it there.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral-7B configurations and controlled reward-granularity, feedback-source, and token-weighting experiments. Reported human-evaluation sampling changes from 50 to 100 instances per dataset, and reward-model training changes from three epochs to two. Appendix C replaces KodCode ROUGE-L with a 90%-overlap metric. These are substantive protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I.1 adds dense-versus-span rewards, human-versus-GPT feedback, and uniform-versus-POS/positional weighting ablations. Appendices K–O add efficiency, span-grounding, failure-mode, and span-length analyses. Existing CoT ablations and training curves are retained and discussed further. The Prime Fibonacci case study from v1 Appendix F.2 is removed.

E5.justification: Figure 5's caption newly states that shaded regions, 'if present,' represent one standard deviation over three random seeds. v1 supplies no equivalent seed or uncertainty information. The plotted curves are retained without clearly visible uncertainty bands, so this is limited reporting rather than evidence that additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive baseline, Mistral, ablation, efficiency, and grounding results. UltraFeedback predicted good/poor span counts change from 736/400 in v1 Table 5 to 932/528 in v2 Table 6; exact matches change from 292/101 to 394/167. KodCode ROUGE-L results of 0.64/0.59 are replaced by 90%-overlap results of 0.67/0.79, which are different-metric results, not directly comparable gains.

T1.justification: The NL-Gradient definition, reward-model objective, PPO objective, and Appendix A derivation are retained. Section 3.5 now explicitly presents the GAE expression already included in v1 Algorithm 4. This expands the main-text explanation without adding a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims of improved alignment, sample efficiency, and interpretability across three task domains remain. v2 adds an explicit conclusion that the gains transfer across model families, supported by the new Mistral evaluation in Section 4.7.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting moderate recall to label imbalance, dense-label failures to noisy rewards, and weighting failures to disrupted span coherence or increased variance. It interprets human disagreement by task subjectivity and discusses tokenization and annotation failures. Appendix G softens v1's scalability concerns using measured overhead and cost, while Appendix M adds the stronger assertion that residual annotation noise has no measurable downstream effect.

D1.justification: New disclosures cover character-span/tokenizer alignment, unmatched-span filtering, baseline preference construction and PRM segmentation, human-evaluation procedures, policy hardware, training times, and annotation budgets. However, the consolidated reward-model table drops v1's maximum prompt/sequence lengths and Adam beta/epsilon values. The code-access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds focused discussion and citations for PRMs, MA-RLHF, SCAR, Beyond Sparse Rewards, and Learning from Natural Language Feedback. Appendix N further discusses PRM applicability. This improves coverage of nearby approaches while retaining the original two-part framing and 'first complete framework' novelty claim.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanations, and several results narratives receive extensive rewriting and terminology cleanup, including clarification that NL-Gradient does not mean literal differentiation through text. Reward-model hyperparameters move from Appendix I into consolidated Appendix D, and later appendices are reorganized. These changes extend beyond the addition of new scientific content.

P2.justification: Main comparison tables gain grouped baseline rows and revised highlighting; three separate PPO hyperparameter tables become one cross-dataset table. New tables display Mistral, reward-design, efficiency, fidelity, and span-length results. Figure 2 gains a fuller color legend and caption, while the existing training curves, preference plots, and coding illustration are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence against alternative learning approaches through DPO, PRM-PPO, and ILF comparisons, alongside Mistral generalization and reward-design ablations. Added timing, cost, and grounding analyses make practical feasibility more assessable. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including unexplained setting changes, omitted hyperparameters, and new numerical inconsistencies: Section 4.3 claims a 6.7-point ROUGE-L gain over PPO, while Table 2 implies 2.9 points. The stronger evaluation materially improves the paper despite these remaining problems.
